reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports that rapid quenching yields an amorphous structure while slower cooling produces crystalline phases, and that phosphorus enhances glass-forming ability. However, the evidence does not report any thermal stability measurements (e.g., DSC crystallization onset temperatures) for the amorphous state, so the premise of improved thermal stability is unsupported.
premises: Ultra-rapid quenching (10^5-10^6 K/s) yields an amorphous structure in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20
Slower cooling (52 K/s, 3018 K/s) produces crystalline or mixed microstructures in this alloy
The amorphous state from rapid quenching exhibits improved thermal stability (higher crystallization onset temperature) compared to slower-cooled states
